name: Auto ISO sensitivity control (maximum ISO, minimum shutter speed)

menu_path.z8: Photo shooting menu > ISO sensitivity settings > Auto ISO sensitivity control / Maximum sensitivity / Minimum shutter speed
menu_path.z5ii: Photo shooting menu > ISO sensitivity settings > Auto ISO sensitivity control / Maximum sensitivity / Minimum shutter speed
menu_path.z50ii: Photo shooting menu > ISO sensitivity settings > Auto ISO sensitivity control / Maximum sensitivity / Minimum shutter speed

one_liner: Camera raises ISO to protect your shutter speed, up to a ceiling you set.
what_it_does: With Auto ISO on, the camera varies ISO to reach correct exposure, never exceeding Maximum sensitivity. In P and A modes it also holds a Minimum shutter speed: ISO climbs before shutter speed is allowed to drop below it. Minimum shutter speed can be a fixed value or Auto, which scales with focal length and can be fine-tuned faster or slower. In M mode with Auto ISO, you fix shutter and aperture and ISO floats, steered by exposure compensation.

options.value: Auto ISO sensitivity control: ON / OFF
options.meaning: ON lets ISO float; OFF keeps the ISO you set.
options.use_when: ON for moving subjects and changing light; OFF for tripod landscape/astro where you want base ISO or a fixed ISO.

options.meaning: Upper ISO limit Auto ISO may use.
options.use_when: Set to the highest ISO you still accept after Lightroom AI Denoise for that body.

options.meaning: Separate ISO ceiling when a flash is fitted.
options.use_when: Keep lower for bounce flash indoors.

options.meaning: P/A modes: ISO rises before shutter falls below this speed (Z50II manual: 1/2000–30 s).
options.use_when: When you know the speed the subject needs (e.g. dancer's hands).

options.meaning: Speed is derived from focal length; fine-tune shifts it faster (toward 'protect against motion') or slower.
options.use_when: Zooms and walk-around use; push fine-tune faster for kids and birds.

when_to_change: Change maximum ISO when light gets dramatically worse (stage, indoors at night) and change minimum shutter when the subject's speed changes, not the lens.

suggested.value: M mode + Auto ISO ON, 1/500–1/640 s, lens wide open, max ISO 12800 (Z8) / 25600 (Z5II); use exposure compensation to bias for spotlit skin
M mode + Auto ISO, 1/2000–1/3200 s for flight, max ISO 6400–12800
Auto ISO OFF, base ISO (64 on Z8, 100 on Z5II/Z50II)
Auto ISO OFF; fixed ISO, shutter ~1/125–1/250 s so the moon stays sharp; expose for the moon
A mode, Auto ISO ON, Minimum shutter Auto fine-tuned 1–2 steps faster, max ISO 12800
Video uses its own ISO settings (Video recording menu > ISO sensitivity settings) - see video file

body_differences: Z8 base ISO 64 (native 64–25600); Z5II native ISO 100–64000; Z50II native ISO 100–51200 (per Nikon spec pages/manual). On the Z5II, 'C' firmware 1.20 changed the range of selectable Minimum shutter speed values (Nikon manual change page; new range not read in this pass). Z8 minimum shutter speed range not verified in this pass.
gotchas: If Maximum sensitivity is reached, shutter speed will drop below your minimum anyway - watch the shutter readout in dark venues.
Minimum shutter speed is ignored in S and M modes; it only governs P and A.
In M + Auto ISO, exposure compensation is how you brighten/darken - it changes ISO, not shutter/aperture.
Active D-Lighting stops working at Hi ISO values, including Hi values chosen by Auto ISO (Z50II manual).
firmware_note: Z5II 'C' firmware 1.20 changed available Minimum shutter speed values. Z8 manual covers firmware 3.10.
research_notes: Z8 and Z5II manual pages load their text via script and could not be read; Z8/Z5II option names inferred from the shared Nikon menu structure (Z8/Z5II table of contents confirms the menu item and location) and the readable Z50II page. Suggested ISO ceilings are field judgement, not measured.

one_liner: Decides which part of the scene the meter trusts when setting exposure.
what_it_does: Metering reads scene brightness and feeds the exposure the camera picks (or the meter you follow in M). Matrix analyses the whole frame; center-weighted favours the middle; spot reads a ~2.5% circle at the active focus point; highlight-weighted biases exposure to keep the brightest areas from clipping. It does not change RAW data, only the exposure chosen.

options.meaning: Whole-frame evaluation using tone distribution, color, composition and distance.
options.use_when: Default for most scenes, family, travel; works best with Active D-Lighting.

options.meaning: Greatest weight on a central circle (size set in Custom setting b5; Average option meters full frame).
options.use_when: Subject fills the centre; also Nikon's suggestion when using filters with a filter factor.

options.meaning: Meters a circle about 2.5% of the frame centred on the current focus point (centre point with Auto-area AF).
options.use_when: Bird against bright sky or dark foliage; meter a specific face.

options.meaning: Weights highlights to reduce highlight clipping, e.g. spotlit stage performers.
options.use_when: Stage dance, moon, white birds in sun; expect a dark rest-of-frame you lift in Lightroom.

when_to_change: Switch from Matrix when a small bright or dark subject sits against a very different background.

suggested.value: Highlight-weighted (protect costume and face highlights under spots)
Matrix for general; Spot or Highlight-weighted for white egrets/gulls in sun
Matrix, check histogram; bracket if needed
Highlight-weighted or Spot on the moon (then check histogram)
Matrix (with b4 Matrix metering face detection ON)
Matrix or Highlight-weighted; spot metering is not offered for video

body_differences: All three offer the same four modes for stills. For video, the Z8 and Z50II specs list Matrix, Center-weighted and Highlight-weighted only (no Spot).
gotchas: Spot follows the focus point; with Auto-area AF it uses the centre - not where the subject is.
Highlight-weighted can underexpose a scene with a small specular highlight (chrome, sun glint).
In M mode with fixed ISO, metering only moves the exposure indicator - it changes nothing by itself.

one_liner: Protects highlights and lifts shadows in high-contrast scenes; can darken RAWs.
what_it_does: ADL tries to keep both highlight and shadow detail in contrasty light, e.g. a shaded face against bright sky or a window view. Nikon describes it working best with Matrix metering. The shadow lift is applied to JPEG/HEIF (and honoured by NX Studio), but the highlight protection comes from the camera choosing a lower exposure, so the RAW file itself is recorded darker than without ADL.

options.use_when: Low or Normal if you want a little highlight protection on RAW.

when_to_change: For a RAW + Lightroom workflow leave it Off and use exposure compensation; turn on only for straight-out-of-camera JPEGs.

Off
